title: New DOJ Report: Indicators of School Crime and Safety, 2005 Shows That State Laws Have No Impact On Student Marijuana Use.

content_html_sanitized:
MarijuanaNews has pointed out repeatedly that the Dutch have a lower rate of marijuana use than DEAland, the UK, France, and many other countries that are very prohibitionist in their policies.
See
 New Dutch Study on "Licit and illicit drug use in the Netherlands" Shows Why International Anti-Dutch Prohibitionist Propaganda Campaign Is Vital to Drug Warriors. How Ideology Works.
and links 

However, I would never have guessed which states have the highest rate of teen use.

According to the DOJ report, New Hampshire has the highest rate of use by students (grades 9 to 12) off school property, 30.6%, even though possession is subject to a year in jail and/or a $2,000 fine.

Neighboring Vermont, where possession is subject to six months in jail, has the highest rate of use on school property, 8%.

Maine, which is a decrim state has a lower rate of use (26.4%) than either of its New England neighbors.

Interestingly, the numbers for Alaska (where possession in the home of four ounces is legal under state law) are almost identical with Arizona.
See
 Lies and Hatred From Former US Attorney In Alaska. As Bad As It Gets.

Also note that Ohio, which is a decrim state, has a slightly lower rate of use than neighboring Indiana, home of arch-prohibitionist, Mark Souder.

These numbers show that we are arresting millions of Americans to support a prohibition that is actually counterproductive.

Indicators of School Crime and Safety, 2005
"Presents data on crime and safety at school from the perspectives of students, teachers, principals, and the general population. A joint effort by the Bureau of Justice Statistics and the National Center for Education Statistics, this annual report examines crime occurring in school as well as on the way to and from school. It also provides the most current detailed statistical information on the nature of crime in schools, school environments, and responses to violence and crime at school."
From http://www.ojp.usdoj.gov/bjs/pub/pdf/iscs05.pdf

To see NORML's analysis of all state laws: http://norml.org/index.cfm?Group_ID=4516
